newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS seeks more comment on natgas royalty plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS seeks more comment on natgas royalty plan.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Thursday it was extending to September 22 the deadline for comments on its new ideas to change the way it calculates natural gas royalties.
Public input on the proposals to streamline royalty payments for natural gas produced on federal lands was originally due July 23.
The agency last April dropped a royalty simplificiation plan which it had negotiated with industry groups over two years, after finding that under the new method it would have earned less money.
Instead, MMS proposed two alternative ways of valuing natural gas which it said would not diminish royalty revenues.
The first option was based on an index price. The second option called for creating a panel that would set the price on which to base royalties.
The government annually collects about $2 billion in natural gas royalties from production on federal leases onshore and offshore.
